lines.text: This toothbrush makes its own electricity, just from you brushing. No battery needed.
It was built by scientists at Peking University's School of Stomatology. That's a dental school.
The secret is the bristles. They're made of a plastic called PVDF, which builds up an electric charge when it bends.
As you brush, that charge sparks reactions in your saliva. They make reactive oxygen molecules that damage bacteria.
In lab tests, the new bristles killed about 53% of a major cavity-causing bacterium. Ordinary nylon bristles? Just 9%.
Then 115 volunteers brushed for three months. The new brush beat nylon on plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding.
The study is in Science Advances, and experts say it needs more testing. But your next toothbrush might zap germs.
